CI TY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
March 12, 2019 7:00 P.M.
Community Room – First Floor
1 West Manchester Boulevard
----------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda other
  than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Cynthia
  Moultrie, representing Savvy School of Beauty, for Special Use
  Permit No. 2018-018 (SP-2018-018) to allow a 7,500 square-foot
  beauty/barber school on a 9,250 square-foot, H-C (Historic
  Core) zoned property at 240 S. Market Street.
  1. Preliminary CEQA Recommendations: Affirm the Categorical
  Exemption EA-CE-2018-148.
  2. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving SP-2018-018 subject to
  conditions.

  b. A public hearing to consider an application by Chibueze Chima
  for Special Use Permit No. 2019-001 (SP-2019-001) to allow a
  4,729 square-foot nightclub and Shared Parking for Infrequent
  Users for an approximately 11,681 square-foot commercial
  building with 51 parking spaces on a 34,581 square-foot MU-1
  (TOD Mixed-Use) zoned property at 446 South Market Street.
  1. Preliminary CEQA Recommendations: Affirm the Categorical
  Exemption EA-CE-2019-003.
  2. Preliminary Recommendations: Adopt Findings and the
  attached resolution approving SP-2019-001 subject to
  conditions.

6.  NON PUBLIC HEARINGS

  a) A non-public hearing to consider an application by David
  Sestak representing Rexford Industrial, L.P. for Design
  Review No. 2019-001 (DR-2019-001) to allow exterior
  alterations to an existing 40,197 square-foot commercial
  building on an MU-2 (Mixed Use-2) zoned property at 220-
  240 Ivy Avenue.
  1. Preliminary Recommendation: Affirm the Categorical
  Exemption EA-CE-2018-121.
  2. Preliminary Recommendation: Approval of DR-2019-001
  subject to conditions.

  b) A non-public hearing to consider an application by Lynette
  Jones-Sawyer, representing Kids’ Castle Child Care Center
  for Design Review No. 2019-002 (DR-2019-002) to allow two
  murals on the exterior of an existing approximately 9,755
  square-foot commercial building and one mural on a
  perimeter wall at 745 N. La Brea Avenue.
  3. Preliminary Recommendation: Affirm the Categorical
  Exemption EA-CE-2019-008.
  4. Preliminary Recommendation: Approval of DR-2019-002
  subject to conditions.

7.  Commission Initiatives

  1
 8.  Adjournment.

If you will require special accommodations, due to a disability,
please contact the Planning Division at (310) 412-5230 or FAX (310)
412-5681, One Manchester Boulevard, Fourth Floor, Inglewood City Hall,
Inglewood, CA 90301. All requests for special accommodations must be
received 48 hours prior to the day of the hearing(s).

"Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor de
llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

In the event that the Special Planning Commission meeting of March 12,
2019 is not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or other
agenda item being considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing
agenda item will automatically be continued to the next regular
Planning Commission meeting.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  TUESDAY, MARCH 12, 2019

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Special Planning
Commission meeting on Tuesday, March 12, 2019, in the Community
Room, on the first floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner David Rice, the meeting was called to
order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Erick Holly
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
Excused
Absence:  Commissioner Terry Coleman

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager stated that she received
communication from Commissioner Terry Coleman, stating he would
not be attending the Special Planning Commission Meeting.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None

(5) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

5a: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2018-018 (SP-2018-018), 240 SOUTH MARKET
STREET.

a. A public hearing to consider an application by Cynthia Moultrie,
  representing Savvy School of Beauty, for Special Use Permit No.
  2018-018  (SP-2018-018)  to  allow  a  7,500  square-foot
  beauty/barber school on a 9,250 square-foot, H-C (Historic Core)
  zoned property at 240 S. Market Street.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Erick Holly asked staff:
 The only reason this item has been brought before the Planning
  Commission is because a Special Use Permit is required for the
  applicant due to the fact that the previous SUP has expired,
  even though it was a beauty college in the past?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, all beauty schools require a
  Special Use Permit.
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 12, 2019

Commissioner David Rice asked staff:
 Are all Beauty Schools required to obtain Special Use approval,
  regardless if it were a Beauty School in the past?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, that is correct.

  No intensity of use with reference to what was there before,
  and are you referencing the school that was there before and
  its use along with it being vacant for more than three years?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, it has been vacant ever since the
  school closed down.

Commissioner Trejo asked:
 Isn’t the reason for the Special Use Permit process also because
  of the Historic Core Zone designation that no similar uses shall
  be allowed in the Historic Core unless there is a Special Use
  Permit process?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the Historic Core requires the SUP
  for the School.
 So the purpose of the SUP is not for the single reason that the
  school has been closed for three years, but for a combination
  of factors such as the vacancy for three years, where it is
  located and the Zoning?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, that is correct.

Commissioner Trejo stated she had several more questions for staff
and made this statement:
 When reviewing projects, there is a process that she follows in
  order to make a determination and decision. Earlier that day
  Commissioner Trejo contacted Planning Staff, Mr. Ikemefuna in
  particular to ask some questions regarding this item and she
  will repeat the same questions to staff now.

  How many blocks does the Historic Core of the Transit Orient
  Development area encompass?
  - Ms. Fewell displayed a map that showed the Historic Core
  Zoning and stated that per the Historic Core Zoning it has
  Market Street through the middle of the zone, covering
  approximately 16 blocks.

  Within that Historic Core, how many Beauty Schools, Beauty
  Supplies, Hair & Nail Salons and Barber Shops are there and how
  many are on Market Street?
  - Twenty-One active Hair, Nail and Barber Shop licensed
  Salons within the Historic Core, with Five on Market
  Street, Ms. Fewell stated.

  With regards to another Beauty School applying to open for
  business and located on Market Street in the Historic Core
  several years back, what is the status of that school?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the Beauty School applied and was
  approved by the Planning Commission in November 2016. They
  have been pursuing their building permits and opened their
  business license in January 2019.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the second Beauty School is not
  located in the Historic Core Zone, but is adjacent to the
  North end of the Historic Core, on Market Street.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about her project.

Ms. Cynthia Moultrie came and addressed the planning commission
about her desires to open the Beauty School.

  2
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 12, 2019
Chairman Springs opened the floor for the planning commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Rice stated:
 He stated he personally knows the applicant and has had business
  dealings with her, yet this will not bear any difference upon
  his decision this evening.
 He asked how many students does the applicant plan on having at
  the school if the application for the Special Use Permit is
  approved?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that the initial startup of running a
  vocational school is costly and it is stipulated that the
  school cannot receive funding or financial aid for the
  first year, until the school is established for one year,
  and this can be very hard on each student that will be
  attending the school and expensive to maintain their first
  year, so she is partnering with organizations who will help
  in sponsoring tuition for the students and will assist them
  in staying at the school.
  - Also, it is a state board of cosmetology requirement in
  order to open a beauty school and receive accreditation,
  that school must start with a minimum of twenty five
  students and maintain them for a period of one year.
  Looking for more students as the business grows.
 He asked the applicant if they feel confident that after being
  open for one year they will receive the accreditation needed to
  run the school?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated with the approval from the Planning
  Commission tonight for the Special Use Permit, on the
  following day she will be obtaining the Post-secondary
  School licensing and accreditation, as they are in the
  process of obtaining all of the accreditations needed to
  open the school.
 He asked what is the parking plan for the students to attend
  the beauty school?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that she looked at the city’s General
  Plan and it spoke about the revitalization of the Downtown
  Inglewood, where it mentions the newly renovated parking
  structure located at Manchester and Locust which is located
  within walking distance from the school, approximately 130
  feet.

Commissioner Trejo stated:
 She too has been in the Inglewood area for many years as well
  and remembers how Downtown Inglewood has changed and is
  continuing to change. Along with the new Transit Oriented
  Development Plan for the City and feels that although the school
  is admirable in theory, feels that a second beauty school was
  not what the new TOD plan had in mind for the Downtown area,
  she feels that the plan calls for more diversity in the downtown
  corridor and stated that she believed that the school would
  serve the community much better in another area of town.
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that the school is not a beauty salon,
  but a school of learning about more than just hair. The
  students are being trained to become cosmetologist, which
  will be a world of knowledge that can take these students
  all over the world. It is a diverse educational service
  center. The Students will have computer literacy, write
  their own business proposal and have a portfolio well put
  together. It is not just a beauty salon.
 How does the school get students prepared to work on live clients
  for cutting hair, etc.?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that in regular beauty colleges,
  clients come in off the street to get haircuts, trims, etc.
  3
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 12, 2019

  That is the concern. If this school were allowed to operate as
  a beauty salon, such as many of the other beauty schools do,
  there would be no diversity of business.
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that since there is a mandate that is
  put upon this beauty school, all of the students will have
  to do their work and training on mannequins. There might
  be some live patrons for special events such as color day,
  hair trim day, but for the most part, mannequins.
  I read that there was mention of volunteers who would come into
  the beauty school, how does that work and how do you obtain the
  volunteers to come in?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that most likely there will be the use
  of social media and word of mouth, request for volunteers
  to come into the beauty school to volunteer their heads to
  receive colorings and cuts by beauty students.

 Commissioner Springs asked:
 Is there a charge for the students to go to this beauty college
  and what is the cost and what does it entail?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated yes, there is tuition. The program
  requires dedicated completed hours of learning - for a
  cosmetologist its 1600 hours, for a barber its 1500 hours,
  for a manicurist it’s a 600 hours and for an esthetician
  its 600 hours. Once those hours are obtained, go before
  the California State Board of Cosmetology and take the
  license exams.
 Is the school open to anyone, including veterans?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated yes, veterans can apply, but it is open
  to anyone with a high school diploma or GED.
 The applicant had mentioned the gentleman who owned the building
  in the past, what was that and did he leave a trust?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated yes, the gentleman’s name was Mr. Yee,
  purchased the building in the early ‘60’s, who happened to
  be a beautician himself and in his trust he demanded that
  the building be used as a beauty school, which is why it
  has sat vacant for the past three years, as many businesses
  have attempted to purchase it or lease it for their own
  use, but Mr. Yee’s trust refused their offers.
 Last question, with regards to you going to social media to
  obtain live customers for the students to do coloring on their
  hair or cuttings, will there be a fee charged to the customers
  to participate in these events?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that normally, such an event has a
  charge applied to it, but if the condition from the
  planning commission is to not have a charge for the service
  by the students, there will be no charge.

Commissioner Rice stated he had one more question:
 When exactly did Mr. Yee purchase the building?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated it was purchased in the 60’s. He leased
  the building to Marinello Beauty School, who lost their
  licensing, thus closing down the school.
 How long did it stay vacant?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that it was empty for approximately
  three years.
 Apparently it is not a hardship for Mr. Yee to keep the building
  empty?
  - Ms. Moultrie said No, but I don’t know for sure.
 Question to staff; the downtown Historic Core and TOD plan for
  the downtown area, is there yet a plan that gives what the
  intentions are for the downtown area? What the layout is going
  to be or look like? Will that include Residential and Business?

  4
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 12, 2019
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the TOD plan allows for a mixed use
  environment in the Historic Core. Yes it will include both.
  Although it does not state the demolishing of older
  constructed buildings, but for the combination of utilizing
  different structures and new construction to create a mixed
  use environment.
  Mr. Yee is not obligated to keeping his building’s use as a
  beauty school, he is choosing to do this on his own?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated yes.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 Mr. Yee will still be required to do what the City wants
  regardless, of what he wants, correct?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated yes.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR:

    Ms. Katherine Buckley – Inglewood Resident
    Ms. Danielle Winston-White – Business Owner
    Ms. Kathy Lacey – Inglewood Resident
    Ms. Joni Quinn – Inglewood Resident

AGAINST:

    None

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any
final comments from the commissioners.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
   What are the hours of operation?
  - Ms. Fewell stated Tuesday thru Saturday, 8:00am–9:00pm.
  This includes both morning and evening classes, which
  does not mean it will run constantly, but that the hours
  the doors will be open.
   How many classes will be running during the days the school
  is open for business?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that during the day, full time
  classes will have 75 Adult Students and during the
  evening part time classes will have 25 Adult Students.
   What are the minimum per day students you can have and the
  desired maximum number of students per day you would like to
  have?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that the minimum per day to open the
  school is 25, the maximum she would like per day would
  be 75 for the full time classes in the morning and 25
  part time in the evening.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant:
   Should the School receive approval from the Planning
  Commission, will the school have both day and evening classes
  everyday Tuesday thru Saturday?
   Ms. Moultrie stated that to start, there will only be the
  morning classes with the initial 25 students and as the
  classes grow, then they will incorporate the evening classes.
  Next, will the applicant have a plan in place when the
  students  feel  that  they  have  reached  a  level  of
  accomplishment, and want to start having live customers hair
  to work on?

  5
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 12, 2019
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that the process of the school is
  the students rank as freshmen, junior and senior. Once
  the student reaches the hours and skillset of a junior,
  they are allowed to start cutting the public’s hair.
    This is the concern that if the applicant is allowed to
  proceed with the school, the desire of the student to want to
  work on the public and risk violating one of the conditions
  and start to turn the school into a beauty salon, is there a
  plan to prevent this?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that this condition has prompted the
  school to reach out to the Cancer Society in order to
  work on the making of wigs, allowing the utilization of
  human hair. Also, the applicant stated there are other
  various organizations that assist people who suffer with
  different forms of hair loss, like alopecia and other
  charities that work with sick children that are in need
  of hair care and this will allow the students to be able
  to work with human hair.
  - Ms. Moultrie stated that these particular organizations
  have already been contacted and have agreed to be part
  of the curriculum of the Beauty School. Ms. Moultrie
  also offered the planning commission a copy of her
  business plan for the school.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant:
   How does the City mandate the parking spaces so that all of
  the other businesses near will have parking?
  - Ms. Moultrie stated in the new General Plan for the City,
  the Public Transportation for the Downtown Core, talks
  about the new parking lot structure that is being
  renovated, which is less than 3.5 blocks from the school,
  definitely within walking distance. The majority of
  people these days do not drive, they utilize Uber, Lyft,
  public transportation like buses, riding their bikes and
  now the parking lot will be for anyone who drives to the
  Beauty College.
  - Technology has changed everyone’s business, even the
  hair business, along with evolving the City and the
  future is now upon us.

Chairman Springs called for the motion.

MOTION:

Commissioner Holly made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2018-148, and to adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2018-018 subject to 10 conditions and was seconded
by Chairman Springs, that Resolution No. 1829

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR
  CYNTHIA MOULTRIE, REPRESENTING SAVVY SCHOOL OF
  BEAUTY, TO ALLOW A BEAUTY/BARBER SCHOOL IN AN
  EXISTING 7,500 SQUARE-FOOT TENANT SPACE ON
  9,250 SQUARE-FOOT, H-C (HISTORIC CORE) ZONED
  PROPERTY LOCATED AT 240 SOUTH MARKET STREET

  6
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 12, 2019
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Holly, Rice, and Chairman Springs.
Nays:  Commissioner Trejo

Ms. Mindy Wilcox explained the appeal process.

5b: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-001 (SP-2019-001), 446 SOUTH MARKET
STREET.

b. A public hearing to consider an application by Chibueze Chima
  for Special Use Permit No. 2019-001 (SP-2019-001) to allow a
  4,729 square-foot nightclub and Shared Parking for Infrequent
  Users for an approximately 11,681 square-foot commercial
  building with 51 parking spaces on a 34,581 square-foot MU-1
  (TOD Mixed-Use) zoned property at 446 South Market Street.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation, along
with the notification that was made in the staff report – The
request for shared parking for infrequent users is no longer
required as upon further analysis, there actually is a surplus of
parking on the subject site based on the TOD Guidelines.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 The stage on the previously approved live entertainment was 75
  square feet, how big is this new one?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated this one is approximately 250 square
  feet and spans across the width of the dance floor and
  also the location of the DJ booth.
 Looking at the elevation plan, it basically only shows a box
  with an entrance. Will there be any requirements for any
  architectural elements or accents?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that staff left that portion out of
  the report as there are no plans for any exterior or
  interior improvements outside of paint at this time, but
  should there be any upgrading of the building, both
  interior or exterior, then the applicant would have to
  come back before the planning commission and staff for a
  Design Review. Right now there will only be a swapping of
  like-for-like of interior items that might be in disrepair
  and this will not trigger the requirement.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 How is there enough parking with only 51 spaces at the site
  for the restaurant, the laundromat and this new club, is the
  City giving any special waivers?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that based on the TOD Parking
  Guidelines which are trying to encourage a more pedestrian
  based usage, there is enough parking.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about his project.

Mr. Chibueze Chima came and addressed the planning commission about
how he started working as a distributor of Cocoa-Beans here in the
United States and how his desire to have an upscale afro-beat club
like he associated with his home town, where everyone can come to
experience the Nigerian Night Life here in Inglewood.
Chairman Springs opened the floor for the planning commission to
address the applicant.

  7
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 12, 2019
Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant several questions:
 Are Cocoa-Beans Chocolate?
  - Mr. Chima stated yes that is correct.
 She asked Mr. Chima if he wanted to establish an upscale new
  club, why hadn’t he made plans to show how he intends on
  renovating the exterior as well as the interior?
  - Mr. Chima stated he wanted to take this process one step
  at a time. First, he wanted to make sure that he would be
  awarded the Special Use Permit in order to open the club.
  Then once he had been given the permission by the Planning
  Commission to open his business, he would start with
  getting new drawings showing his next interior and exterior
  designs and upgrades.
 She also asked where did he get his experience in nightclub
  operations, was it here in the United States or back home in
  Nigeria, if here, then where and how many years’ experience did
  he have in running his own club?
  - Mr. Chima stated that he obtained his experience while he
  was back home, but he also spun records here in the states
  and at several local clubs on various nights.
 Commissioner Trejo asked which club here in Inglewood?
  - Mr. Chima stated yes here in Inglewood he is called a
  Promoter and he has worked in particular with the owner
  at the Savoy on La Brea, where he promotes during the
  weekends and special events, now the Savoy is the club to
  go to for that Nigerian Experience.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant:
 How many days of the week will the club be open and what will
  the hours of operation be?
  - Mr. Chima stated that the club will be open during the
  daytime from Tuesday thru Sunday’s opening at 4:00pm and
  during the day the Bar will be open for game watching, a
  meal, or drinks.
 Now you do not have a kitchen in the club, but you do have a
  prep area? Where would the food come from and what about the
  eatery next door?
  - Mr. Chima stated that he has made arrangements for food to
  be catered in and will be kept in the prep area, along with
  utilizing Rosalie’s Eatery next door who has agreed to also
  offer her kitchen for food.
 Last, Chairman Springs stated what about the laundromat that is
  also next door and what about the fact that it is opened until
  11:00pm, what about the customers that will be utilizing the
  Laundry mat and needing parking spaces?
  - Mr. Chima stated that there is plenty of parking in the
  lot and the use by the laundromat is very minimal in the
  evenings and there is no conflict there.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR:

    Ms. Chioma Oparaocha Chima – Business Partner
    Mr. Azuga Egua – Business Owner
    Mr. Michal Fadioya – Business Owner

AGAINST:

    None

  8
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 12, 2019
Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any
final comments from the commissioners.
